dicas.texto: Para transformar uma fração em porcentagem, o denominador deve ser 100. Se o número precisa aumentar, qual operação matemática faz isso?
Você quer chegar em 100. Como o 25 é menor que 100, você deve multiplicar o 25 por um número para atingir a meta.
Pense na tabuada do 25: 25 x 1 = 25, 25 x 2 = 50... quantas vezes o 25 cabe dentro do 100?
Você está quase lá! Se você tem 25 e quer chegar em 100, o fator de escala é o número que, multiplicado por 25, resulta em 100. Qual é esse número?

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado com as partes da tarefa e, abaixo, uma TABELA de razões com três linhas — Total, Part 1 e Part 2 — e, em cada linha, quatro grupos de células: (1) a razão ORIGINAL (numerador e denominador, dois campos); (2) a coluna "Operation": dois seletores em que o aluno escolhe × ou ÷ (um para o numerador, um para o denominador); (3) a coluna "Scale Factor": dois campos com o fator aplicado ao numerador e ao denominador; (4) o RESULTADO: um campo para o numerador da razão equivalente, cujo denominador já vem impresso como 100 (isto é, a porcentagem), e um campo para o valor da porcentagem. Botão Hint; botão Done. Cada célula preenchida é um passo do aluno; a tabela inteira tem 24 células a completar.

dicas.texto: A ratio compares the number of dogs with the kennel's total cage capacity.
For each row, place the number of dogs in the numerator and the total cage capacity in the denominator.
Use the kennel capacity as the denominator in every row, then enter the corresponding dog count as the numerator.
Complete the Total, Part 1, and Part 2 rows by entering each dog count over the same capacity value.
Percent means a ratio out of one hundred, so every denominator must become 100.
Find the number that multiplies the original denominator to make 100, then use that same factor on the numerator.
Because 25 is multiplied to reach 100, choose the multiplication symbol rather than division in all six operation selectors.
Enter the single scale factor that turns 25 into 100 in every scale-factor cell, and select multiplication for every operation.
Equivalent ratios require multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same factor.
For each row, multiply its original numerator by the scale factor shown in the table.
Apply the multiplication separately to 25, 28, and 7, keeping the rows in the same order.
Calculate each product using the factor 4, then enter the three products in the Total, Part 1, and Part 2 result-numerator cells.
A percentage tells how many parts there are out of 100.
When the denominator is 100, read the numerator as the percentage number.
Use the three numerators in the result column to choose the matching percentage for each row.
Match each result numerator with the same number followed by the percent sign, then select Done to submit the completed table.

exercicio.statement:
Abhi works at a kennel that has cages for 25 dogs, assuming one dog per cage. Sometimes, it gets very busy and he has to put multiple dogs in the cages as needed.

Part 1) If 28 dogs were dropped off, the kennel was filled to what percent capacity?

Part 2) If instead 7 puppies were boarded, how busy was the kennel in terms of percent capacity? Part 1) If 28 dogs were dropped off, the kennel was filled to what percent capacity?
Part 2) If instead 7 puppies were boarded, how busy was the kennel in terms of percent capacity?
